hard_constraints: Every required collection point must be assigned to a route or explicitly marked unavailable/unserved.
A route must not exceed the assigned vehicle's usable capacity without a recorded unloading trip.
Collection windows and shift end times must be respected.
A planned stop is not counted as collected until a completion event is recorded.
Failed stops and breakdowns must trigger reassignment or an explicit unresolved exception.

warnings: The supplied files describe Pune, not the hypothetical city/9-zone/40-ward example. The master file uses source-supported Pune data.
There are 42 ward records in the ward-level sources, not 40. Ward 42 has a composite/ambiguous zone label and is left unassigned rather than guessed.
Household totals and D2D collection household counts differ substantially; they are stored as separate source measures and should not be treated as interchangeable.
The waste-segregation household count equals the total household count for all source rows; verify whether this reflects real 100% segregation or a data-entry/reporting issue.
Vehicle fleet count is populated for only a subset of the source records; the single reported count must not be interpreted as a citywide total or copied to every ward.
The disposal-site source contains only one populated destination record, with no coordinates.
Historical recycling values are strings such as '165 MT/day' despite a column label mentioning million tonnes. Values are preserved raw pending unit verification.

No household-level, commercial-point-level or geocoded bin data was supplied. This dataset supports ward-level dashboards and planning, but cannot by itself calculate real road-by-road optimal truck routes or guarantee zero missed stops.
Blank cells in the original spreadsheets were not filled with invented values. Missing operational values remain null.
